$comment: The finding classes the trial has surfaced, one per beads issue. gate.mjs --write classifies a new failing step by the first class whose matchers fit and writes the class's note into trial-baseline.json; a failure no class fits stays unclassified and keeps the gate red. A class is removed here, with its baseline rows, in the PR that fixes the issue.

classes.note: barwise's own per-dialect DDL export read back through import sql is not a fixed point. Since barwise-jjd, import sql reads CREATE TABLE through the DDL importer, and on every customer the read-back loses exactly as many elements as the sprint-1 model-roundtrip:ddl row does -- the same loss, reached through a second command (barwise-dnm). Graded since Copilot pointed out that the sprint-4 read-back validated structure only, on PR #509.

docs/CLI.md shows lineage impact --element with a name; the option takes an id and a name silently matches nothing, exit 0 (barwise-5m9). Cannot close before barwise-ofb, since with no sources recorded the id gives the same empty answer.

Consequence of barwise-dnm: import sql reads DDL through the DDL importer (barwise-jjd), so the model it produces loses value types and fact types on the export-and-reimport round trip as the DDL importer's does. Closes with the parent.
Consequence of barwise-dnm: the DDL export of the imported model does not read back to the same model -- value types and fact types are lost beyond the declared loss set. Closes with the parent.

barwise-oph reached from the sprint-1 round trip: NORMA has no place for the population sample flag, so the re-imported populations count as real, their instances enter the object universe, and every mandatory role they do not play reports a violation. The model that was exported validates clean.

The default OpenAPI export writes a /* comment */ header when the model has diagnostics (which it always has after barwise-lh9), so the .json is not JSON and the importer returns an empty model with exit 0 (barwise-sxh).
OpenAPI export then import drops data-type lengths, definitions and value constraints on every value type and loses subtypes beyond the declared loss set (barwise-a0h).
DDL export then import is not a fixed point: annotated exports re-import with zero fact types, unannotated ones lose value types and fact types beyond the declared loss set (barwise-dnm).
dbt export then import loses value types, definitions, subtypes and objectification beyond the declared loss set (barwise-vsp).
NORMA export then import re-homes subset, exclusion and external uniqueness constraints onto sibling fact types and drops definitions, on an importer documented as nearly lossless (barwise-ro8).

Reading barwise's own NORMA export back yields a model that fails barwise's own validation with population/mandatory-violation. The cause is the lost `sample: true` flag: NORMA has no seat for a sample instance, so the populations come back significant, their instances enter the object universe, and every mandatory role they must play reports a violation (barwise-oph). Restoring only that flag takes the round-tripped model from 49 errors to 0.
diff reports this rename as a removal plus an addition with no synonym candidate while other renames in the same history are reported as candidates (barwise-rkm).

The code importers skip any class whose name is on a fixed utility list (Event, Request, Result, Error, Context, ...) with exit 0 and no warning naming it (barwise-tn4). C06 has a domain class Event; the import returns ScanEvent and ShipmentEvent but no Event. Hidden until the import oracle stopped accepting a name as present because another name ended with it.
The Kotlin importer returns an empty model for data classes and sealed classes with constructor properties, exit 0, no warning naming a class (barwise-dyq).
merge exits 1 with 'Merge produced 1 structural error(s)' on a fact-type rename and does not say which error (barwise-nqd).
The release CLI bundle cannot resolve the packaged gym catalog (import.meta.url is empty under cjs) and fails with a Node path error (barwise-fbi).

Edit distance to acceptance on C05's SAP DDL. MAT_IS_PRODUCED_AT_WERK_IN_CHA is WorkOrder's table, keyed on CHARG_ID alone (the kernel's uniqueness over the batch role), which is a key that is also a foreign key: an entity identified through another entity, which core cannot express (barwise-3pc). The import keeps the key and drops the reference, so no fact type connects Material and Plant. Was barwise-2z1 until composite-key-tables.spec.md, which covers keys of two or more roles.

Edit distance to acceptance on C03's claims dbt project. The coverage model references PolicyPeriod, now keyed on two columns, through two relationships tests; the dbt importer reads them as two references, so the composite-key rule sees two columns beside the key and objectifies instead of reading the ternary 'Coverage applies to Risk under PolicyPeriod' (barwise-tjg).

Edit distance to acceptance on a dbt project. Nothing is declared not_expressible for dbt: a singular test is SQL, so even a ring constraint can be stated (PR #575 review). What remains are checks the round trip does not carry: rings, multi-column uniqueness, warn-severity rules, subtypes, relationship roles, composite-key ternaries (barwise-nkn).
Edit distance to acceptance on a Kotlin repo: the persona's checks fail because the Kotlin importer returned an empty model (barwise-dyq). A consequence row; closes with that importer issue.

barwise-nm4: the NORMA importer drops every internal uniqueness constraint that no fact references, while keeping the mandatory ones, so the imported model allows what the source forbids. Exit 0, confidence high, no warning. A consequence row; closes with that importer issue.

A blind spot, not a finding: barwise registers no Avro importer, so the lane cannot read its own Avro export back, and no other step checks it. Avro export correctness is unverified until barwise-s4x gives it a check that can fail.

Edit distance to acceptance on an OpenAPI artifact. Checks OpenAPI cannot state (rings, deontic rules, composite and value-side uniqueness, n-ary uniqueness) are declared not_expressible on the personas (barwise-1079). What remains is the importer ignoring discriminator subtypes (barwise-nul).
